subject: Milestone-linked term proposal with optional auto-renew
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — milestone-linked term proposal

Sara —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our call I’m sending a compact proposal to make the renewal aligned with measurable usage milestones while keeping flexibility on capacity. High level:

- Term: 36 months (three-year) with staged capacity increases at month 6, month 12 and month 24.
- Usage-linked triggers: each staged increase is conditional on a usage trigger (avg monthly tokens or API calls) or a mutual KPI (feature adoption) — we can define the exact metric in the SOW.
- Optional auto-renew: a 60-day opt-out window prior to renewal; if neither party opts out, the contract auto-renews for a successive 12-month period at a pre-agreed rate band.
- Co-terming: we can align final contract boundary with Acme’s fiscal year (Jan 1) via proration on the initial invoice.
- Pricing: tiered unit price with an early-burst credit for the first 60 days after any staged increase.

I attached a short term sheet and a kickoff plan for the knowledge ingestion (KI-activation-plan.xlsx) so your engineers can see the onboarding milestones. If this direction looks reasonable, can you confirm: (1) whether Acme prefers co-term to Jan 1, (2) who in procurement should receive the formal term-sheet, and (3) any internal constraints on auto-renew?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk the SOW details.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: term-sheet-v1.pdf (pdf), KI-activation-plan.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — milestone-linked term proposal

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick asks from our side:

- We like the milestone-linked approach but would need the ability to accelerate a staged increase if usage breaks through the trigger early — is there an expedited bump process?
- Can you confirm billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether early bursts are invoiced as credits or separate line items? Our procurement team (cc’d) needs those details for forecasting.
- Co-terming to Jan 1 should be fine — we may prefer a single annual invoice aligned to our fiscal year.

I’ll loop in procurement formally — procurement@acmehealth.com is our billing contact. Also, can you share an example proration illustration for a mid-quarter co-term?

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Product Ops
Acme Health

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — milestone-linked term proposal

Sara —

Thanks — absolutely yes on the accelerated bump. Proposed mechanics:

- Accelerated bump: if usage exceeds the staged trigger by 25% for any 14-day rolling window, Acme can request the staged increase immediately; Redwood will provision burst capacity within 7 business days and invoice the delta pro-rated from the effective bump date.
- Early-burst accounting: the first 60 days after any staged increase are covered by an early-burst credit (applied to the invoice as a negative line item). After that, normal tiered pricing applies.
- Billing cadence: default quarterly invoicing aligned to your fiscal co-term (Jan 1) is feasible. We’ll provide a sample proration table in the formal term sheet.

I’ve updated the term sheet and attached proposal_v2.pdf with a sample proration illustration and a worked example of the accelerated bump. If this looks good, we’ll prepare the SOW amendment and route to legal + procurement.

Would you like us to support a single annual invoice instead of quarterly? We can switch to annual invoice if procurement prefers, with the same proration behavior on co-terming.

Cheers,
Kimberly

Attachments: proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme — early-burst / co-term ask (RDW-5931)

Team — quick internal summary and ask:

Acme is receptive to the 36-month milestone-linked structure but wants (a) the option to accelerate a staged increase if usage spikes and (b) co-terming to Jan 1 with annual invoicing. They’ve cc’d procurement for billing.

Request: can we approve a 7-business-day provisioning SLA for accelerated bumps and provide an early-burst credit for first 60 days after any staged increase? They may ask for a modest onetime onboarding discount tied to signing the SOW amendment by July 23.

I’ve attached the latest proposal (proposal_v2.pdf). Deal: RDW-5931. If legal needs to weigh in, I can route to Marissa for a redline.

– Kimberly
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme — early-burst / co-term ask (RDW-5931)

Kimberly —

Approve the operational approach with these conditions:

1) Early-burst credit limited to the first 60 days post-bump and capped at a 25% of the incremental month spend.
2) Provisioning SLA for accelerated bumps set to 7 business days but subject to capacity windows; include a fallback to a compatible model variant if we cannot meet a GPU allocation within that window.
3) Any onboarding discount must be approved by Revenue Ops; cap at a one-time 5% on the first-year committed amount.

We’ll need legal to prepare a short SOW amendment (DocuSign preferred). I’ll loop Marissa once Kimberly confirms final numbers.

— Karthik
From: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 13:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — milestone-linked term proposal

Kimberly / Procurement —

This looks good to us. Acme agrees to the accelerated bump mechanics and the 60-day early-burst credit (subject to the cap Karthik noted). We’d like the SOW amendment routed to procurement@acmehealth.com and Sara.Gomez@acmehealth.com for signature. Co-term to Jan 1 and annual invoicing preferred.

Please send the final term-sheet and DocuSign link and we’ll aim to sign by July 23.

Thanks — excited to keep scaling together.

Sara

Acme Health
